title: Ecosystem
seo_title: Ecosystem Class 12 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 12)
standard_text: Ecosystems: patterns, components; productivity and decomposition; energy flow; pyramids of number, biomass, energy.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 12 Ecosystem: components, productivity, decomposition, food chains, energy flow and the 10% law, and ecological pyramids. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.
body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem has biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers) and abiotic components. Primary productivity is the rate at which producers make organic matter; NPP = GPP − R. Decomposition (fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification, mineralisation) recycles nutrients and is fastest when warm and moist.

Energy flows one way from the Sun through producers to consumers; at each step only about 10% passes on (the 10% law), so food chains are short and the pyramid of energy is always upright. Pyramids of number and biomass can be inverted, as for biomass in the sea.

Example

Producers 10,000 J. Secondary consumers?

× 0.1²

Answer: 100 J

Example

GPP 5000, R 2000. NPP?

GPP − R

Answer: 3000

Common mistakes

  • Saying energy is recycled in ecosystems.
  • Thinking every pyramid is upright.
  • Adding respiration to get NPP.

faq.q: Why is the pyramid of energy always upright?
faq.a: Energy is lost as heat at each level, so each higher level always has less energy.
Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next.

items.q: Producers in a food chain fix 4,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
